releases.body:
BlackRock's Nick Nefouse Discusses Guaranteed Income, the Evolution of 401(k)s, and the Future of Retirement Security

WASHINGTON, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The National Institute on Retirement Security (NIRS) today released Episode 7 of its Retirement in America podcast, "Making the 401(k) Look More Like a Pension: The Future of Lifetime Retirement Income."

The episode features Nick Nefouse, Global Head of Retirement Solutions and Head of LifePath at BlackRock, joining podcast host and NIRS Executive Director Dan Doonan to discuss how retirement plans are evolving to help Americans turn their savings into reliable income throughout retirement.

Retirement in America is available on the NIRS website, YouTube and all major podcast platforms.

For decades, traditional pensions provided workers with predictable monthly income for life. But as private-sector employers have shifted toward 401(k) plans, workers increasingly bear responsibility not only for saving and investing, but also for determining how to make their savings last throughout retirement. The podcast conversation explores how innovations in retirement plan design could bring some of the most valuable features of traditional pensions into today's 401(k) system.

"Saving enough for retirement is only part of the challenge. Americans also need help turning those savings into income they can count on for the rest of their lives," Doonan said. "Nick offers an interesting perspective on how the retirement industry is rethinking 401(k) plans to address that challenge. As more Americans retire without traditional pensions, addressing this gap will reduce financial-related stress in retirement by adding back some of the certainty that so many workers have lost in recent decades."

A central focus of the discussion is BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck®, a retirement investment solution that integrates access to a guaranteed lifetime income stream provided by third-party insurers into a target-date strategy. As participants approach retirement, the strategy gradually builds an allocation to group annuity contracts, which participants may elect to convert into a lifetime income stream while keeping the remainder of their savings invested and accessible. Nefouse explains how this approach seeks to provide greater income certainty in retirement while reducing the need for workers to make complex investment and income-planning decisions on their own.

Among the topics discussed in the episode:

  • Making 401(k)s work more like pensions. How retirement plans are evolving beyond accumulating savings to help workers generate dependable income throughout retirement, incorporating professional investment management and features traditionally associated with pensions.
  • The challenge of spending retirement savings. Why retirees often hesitate to draw down their savings, even when they have accumulated substantial assets, and how predictable income can help them make more confident spending decisions.
  • The role of employers and retirement plan design. How workplace plans can offer institutional investment management, fiduciary oversight and potentially lower costs, along with the challenges employers face in adopting new retirement income solutions.
  • The future of retirement investing. The potential role of private-market investments, participant education and public policy in helping retirement plans deliver better long-term outcomes.
  • BlackRock's LifePath Paycheck strategy. How the strategy integrates access to guaranteed lifetime income into a target-date strategy, with the ability to convert a portion of the portfolio into a lifetime income stream, providing a paycheck for life in retirement, while keeping remaining assets invested and accessible.

Retirement in America is a NIRS podcast exploring the economic, workforce and policy issues shaping Americans' retirement security.

The National Institute on Retirement Security is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization established to contribute to informed policymaking by fostering a deep understanding of the value of retirement security to employees, employers, and the economy as a whole. Located in Washington, D.C., NIRS membership includes financial services firms, employee benefit plans, trade associations, and other retirement service providers.

releases.body:
Founder David Plotz hands leadership to longtime business partner as City Cast, with 1.5 million listeners and readers across 13 cities, reimagines local media for how people live now

WASHINGTON, Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- City Cast, the local media network connecting people to the cities they love, has named co-founder Andi McDaniel as chief executive officer. McDaniel succeeds founder David Plotz, who is departing after six years of building City Cast from a two-person startup into a 13-city network reaching 1.5 million people. McDaniel will guide City Cast's next phase: expanding audiences, accelerating revenue growth, and embracing new platforms.

Plotz and McDaniel founded City Cast in 2020 on a simple belief: people are more connected than ever, and somehow less connected to the places they live. As local newspapers, community institutions, and shared rituals have faded, City Cast set out to become the new thread — a daily conversation about what's happening in your city, and why it matters. City Cast has expanded from daily audio podcasts and newsletters into a fully multiplatform local media company, with video on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, live events, and Neighbors, City Cast's paid membership program. City Cast has also recently established a 16-person local newsroom for its Washington, DC outlet.

"Building City Cast has been the proudest achievement of my career," Plotz said. "We've created something from nothing, growing from two employees to 122 and building a company that's ambitious and experimental, with a culture that's joyful and kind. Andi has been central to that work from the beginning, and she's exactly the visionary leader City Cast needs for what comes next."

At a time when local newspapers are shrinking and media companies are cutting staff, City Cast is one of the few local networks growing across multiple cities. The company recently posted its strongest revenue quarter. Most of City Cast's audience is between 21 and 44 — a cohort traditional local media has struggled to reach.

"People care as much as ever about what's happening where they live. They just want it delivered in a way that fits their lives," said McDaniel. "City Cast is showing that it's possible to reach younger audiences with local news and information they care about and are willing to pay for."

McDaniel has shaped City Cast's editorial voice, talent and brand since its launch, first as chief creative officer and recently as interim CEO. Before City Cast, McDaniel was chief content officer at WAMU, NPR's Washington station, where she led the development of the national daily program 1A, launched a podcast division and oversaw a period in which the station's audience grew larger, younger and more diverse and its revenue nearly doubled.

"City Cast is building something new in local media, reaching younger audiences on the platforms where they spend the most time," said Tim O'Shaughnessy, President and Chief Executive Officer of Graham Holdings Company, City Cast's parent company. "I am thrilled that Andi McDaniel will lead City Cast in its next chapter, where we aim to turn our extensive local reach into an excellent business. Andi's ability to understand what local communities want, her extensive background leading editorial organizations, and her drive to build new business models give her the perfect trifecta to be the next CEO of City Cast."

About City Cast

City Cast is a network of local media outlets making podcasts, newsletters, and social content in 13 U.S. cities.Through daily conversations, local news, and recommendations for making the most of city life, City Cast helps residents stay informed, curious and connected. City Cast operates in 13 cities: Austin, Chicago, Denver, Las Vegas, Madison, Nashville, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Portland, Salt Lake City, Seattle, the Twin Cities and Washington, D.C. City Cast is part of Graham Holdings Company. Learn more at citycast.fm.

NEW YORK, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Omnicom Media, an Omnicom (NYSE: OMC) Connected Capability, has been named a "Leader" among global media management services providers in a new analysis from leading research and advisory firm Forrester.

Published today, The Forrester Wave™: Media Management Services, Q4 2026 evaluated the 12 most significant media management service providers against 19 criteria specific to current offering and strategy. Designed to help CMO professionals select the right provider for their needs, the report assesses the media groups under three designations: Leaders, Strong Performers, and Contenders.

With the highest possible scores (5) across seven criteria, Omnicom Media was one of three of the 12 providers evaluated to receive designation as a "Leader". Under the current offering category, OMG received 5/5 scores in four of the 13 criteria, including data/marketing sciences, commerce media, media buying, and principal- media buying. Additionally, OMG received the highest possible scores in three out of the six criteria within the strategy category, including innovation, partner ecosystem, and global delivery strategy.

TORONTO and ST. JOHN'S, NL, Nov. 2, 2026 /CNW/ -- Creative Currency, the Toronto-based advertising agency and content studio, today announced it has acquired Launch Media, a fast-growing Newfoundland and Labrador marketing agency. As part of the firm's first new acquisition, Creative Currency named St. John's its Atlantic Canada headquarters.

Launch Media founder and President Chris Dunne joins Creative Currency as Vice President, Atlantic Canada. He will lead the firm's growth across Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island, with a mandate to expand and scale clients, talent and revenue in the region.

The acquisition supercharges Creative Currency's existing Halifax team as the agency now has two Atlantic Canada offices and a deeper bench on the ground, giving clients across all four provinces more capacity, faster turnaround and local insight.

"Atlantic Canada is key growth market for us and we have always known that to win in this market you need to show up, in person and on the ground," said Dennis Matthews, President of Creative Currency. "Chris is a builder who knows what it takes to win in Newfoundland and Labrador and across the region. He took Launch from one client to a roster with national reach in three years. That's the ambition we look for, and we're proud to have him and his team on board."

A growth story on both sides of the deal

Launch Media opened in 2023 with a single client. In three years it has built a team of 10 designers, content creators, digital marketers and strategists, with clients in automotive, ocean technology, logistics, financial services and food, and a growing national footprint. That growth brought Launch to an inflection point. The next stage demands scale: deeper creative and production capacity, national media buying, and the backing to compete for larger mandates. Joining Creative Currency delivers all three.

For Creative Currency, ranked No. 1 on Adweek's 2024 Fastest Growing Agencies list, the transaction adds an established book of business, a proven team and a permanent footprint on the ground in one of Canada's most dynamic regional markets. Launch Media clients gain Creative Currency's national creative, content and public affairs capabilities.

"We built Launch to punch above our weight. Now we don't have to," said Chris Dunne, Vice President, Atlantic Canada. "Our clients keep the people they know and gain the firepower of a national agency. Our team gets a bigger stage without leaving home. St. John's just became an Atlantic headquarters, and we intend to earn it."

An extended offering from Enterprise Canada

Creative Currency's sister agency, Enterprise Canada, also benefits from this transaction by gaining client relationships and increased capacity on the ground. For more about Enterprise Canada, a leading national strategic communications firm: https://enterprisecanada.com

"We are proud to welcome Chris and the Launch team to our broader full-service offering," said David Tarrant, Vice President, National Strategic Communications and Practice Lead, Atlantic Canada at Enterprise Canada and Strategic Advisor, Creative Currency. "Since Enterprise Canada opened our initial office in Halifax in 2021, our Atlantic Canadian team has grown by combining the very best talent in the entire country with a deep understanding of the local marketplace, delivering a unique offering. Creative Currency opening a new headquarters in my home province of Newfoundland and Labrador is an exciting next step in this journey."

What the deal means

  • Headquarters: St. John's becomes Creative Currency's Atlantic Canada HQ, informally known as CC Atlantic, alongside Halifax to drive growth across all four provinces.
  • Leadership: Chris Dunne is appointed Vice President, Atlantic Canada, reporting to President Dennis Matthews.
  • Team: Launch Media's full team joins Creative Currency.
  • Clients: Launch Media clients keep the team they know, now backed by a national agency.
  • Strategy: This is the first step in a disciplined growth plan. Creative Currency will keep evaluating opportunities to add talent, capabilities and markets across Canada.

About Creative Currency

Creative Currency is a Toronto-based, full-service advertising agency and content studio working at the intersection of advertising and public affairs. Spun out of Enterprise Canada in 2021, the agency brings together creative thinking, strategic communications and a deep understanding of public policy to help brands, organizations and causes tell compelling stories, shape public opinion and inspire action. It was ranked No. 1 on Adweek's 2024 Fastest Growing Agencies list. Creative Currency has offices across Canada, in St. John's, Halifax, Ottawa, Toronto, Hamilton, Calgary and Vancouver. NEW YORK, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Better Business Advice has named CapCut a top choice in a 2026 review of AI software for social media marketing, highlighting support for campaign planning, advertising concepts, and post-launch creative revisions. The review examines how businesses can use AI-assisted tools to develop promotional materials around marketing objectives rather than simply produce more social media content.

The recognition addresses a practical challenge for small businesses and lean marketing teams. A single promotion may require multiple advertising angles, visual formats, approvals, and adjustments after launch. CapCut supports several stages of that process through three creative tools.

Best AI Software for Social Media Marketing:

  • Seedream - CapCut's AI image generator that turns written marketing briefs into visual concepts, mood boards, and promotional image drafts.
  • Seedance 2.0 - CapCut's AI video generator that creates motion-based drafts for advertising hooks, product demonstrations, launch teasers, and campaign storyboards.
  • AI Image Extender - CapCut's image editing tool that expands backgrounds to help adapt campaign visuals for different layouts and advertising placements.

Why CapCut Is a Practical Choice for Social Media Marketing

Social media campaigns begin with a business objective, whether generating leads, increasing store visits, or driving online sales. Effective creative assets need to communicate a relevant benefit, present a clear offer, and support the intended action.

Better Business Advice recognizes CapCut for helping translate those priorities into visual materials. Seedream supports early direction, Seedance 2.0 supports promotional video concepts, and AI Image Extender supports subsequent adaptations. The combined workflow is particularly relevant when production resources are limited, or campaigns require frequent updates.

The advantage is flexibility across campaign stages, not automatic marketing decisions. Businesses still determine audience targeting, offers, budgets, and performance goals.

How Seedream Helps Turn Marketing Briefs Into Visual Campaign Concepts

A product can support several promotional messages. A travel mug, for example, might be positioned around everyday commuting, outdoor activities, or temperature retention. Each approach calls for a different visual treatment.

Seedream converts prompts into concept images that can be compared before a photo shoot or final design is commissioned. Better Business Advice identifies three elements that make those prompts more useful:

  • Audience and objective: Define the customer and desired response.
  • Offer and message: Specify the benefit, promotion, or customer problem.
  • Creative direction: Establish setting, tone, branding requirements, and format.

This structure helps reviewers judge visual drafts against the campaign brief rather than personal preference alone. Generated imagery still requires checks for product accuracy, brand consistency, and realistic advertising claims before publication.

How Seedance 2.0 Supports Testing Different Social Media Ad Messages

Video advertising often depends on the opening message. A demonstration highlighting a product feature may appeal to a different audience than a lifestyle-led promotion of the same item.

Seedance 2.0 can turn alternative written concepts into motion drafts for storyboards, launch teasers, and product demonstrations. That capability makes exploring distinct advertising hooks more practical before committing to full production.

The Better Business Advice review also connects creative variations with A/B testing. A controlled comparison might change the opening scene while keeping the audience, offer, and landing page consistent. Marketers can then assess whether the creative difference affects the intended result.

CapCut creates visual materials; advertising platforms supply performance data. Relevant measures include click-through rate for traffic campaigns, qualified leads for inquiry campaigns, and cost per purchase for online sales. High view counts alone do not establish advertising effectiveness.

How AI Image Extender Helps Refine Campaign Assets After Launch

Campaign results frequently call for targeted changes rather than complete redesigns. A successful product visual might need a wider format, while a closely cropped image might require extra room for a headline.

AI Image Extender generates space around an existing image, helping adjust composition for another advertising placement while retaining the main subject. The revised asset still needs inspection for visual accuracy and commercial-use requirements.

Better Business Advice outlines a performance-informed revision cycle: review the objective, identify the weak point, change a relevant element, and compare the new version. Low click-through rates may suggest a clearer hook. Strong clicks but weak sales could instead indicate an issue with pricing or the landing page.

The distinction prevents unnecessary creative changes and keeps revisions linked to the campaign's actual goal.

What Better Business Advice's Recognition Means for Marketing Teams

Better Business Advice identifies CapCut as a top choice because the platform supports three connected needs: campaign concept development, promotional message exploration, and practical visual adaptation. These capabilities can help small businesses and ecommerce teams manage recurring promotions without treating every creative variation as a separate production project.

The full review can be read at the Better Business Advice website.

CapCut is an AI-powered photo and video editing platform designed to make high-quality video creation accessible across devices. The platform supports creators, businesses, and everyday users with tools for video editing, AI video generation, captions, templates, audio, and visual editing. CapCut is available across mobile, web, desktop, and iPad experiences, helping users create, edit, and prepare video content for social media, marketing, education, and personal projects.

releases.body:
Founder and CEO Kathryn Wilson also named one of the Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026

BOSTON, Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VUE Health, an independent healthcare advertising agency that helps emerging biopharma companies bring breakthrough therapies to market, has been named Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026 by Healthcare Business Review. The publication featured VUE Health as its cover story, "VUE Health: The Creative Architects Behind Tomorrow's Breakthrough Medicines." In a second milestone, VUE Health Founder and CEO Kathryn Wilson has been named one of the Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026.

Key facts about VUE Health

  • Recognition: Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026 (Healthcare Business Review); Founder and CEO Kathryn Wilson named one of the Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026 (MSN)
  • What VUE Health is: A healthcare advertising and medical communications agency focused on helping innovative therapies reach the people who need them
  • Who VUE serves: Emerging biopharma companies commercializing therapies in oncology, rare disease, central nervous system conditions, and novel delivery technologies
  • Leadership: Kathryn Wilson, Founder and CEO; Vikram Kanda, PhD, Chief Medical Officer and Partner

Why VUE Health Was Named Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026

The Healthcare Business Review recognition cites VUE Health's ability to combine deep scientific expertise, strategic insight, and creative execution to help innovative therapies move from development into meaningful patient impact.

VUE Health was built on a simple premise: put senior expertise back into the work. Unlike the traditional model, in which senior executives win the business and hand it to junior teams, VUE Health's experienced strategists, scientists, medical professionals, and creative leaders stay closely involved with clients throughout the commercialization journey. Clients have come to call VUE Health the "non-agency agency": no layers and senior people who work as true partners.

What sets VUE Health apart

  • Science at the foundation. A multidisciplinary medical team of PhDs and PharmDs works alongside strategy and creative, so scientific understanding stays central to every program
  • Sync Sprint methodology. VUE Health's approach can bring a product or program to market in as little as 90 days when circumstances demand it, starting with deep scientific immersion, market understanding, and strategic alignment before execution accelerates
  • Proven launch impact. For a rare disease therapy for Castleman disease, which was facing limited awareness and widespread misdiagnosis, VUE Health prepared for launch in about 90 days. Its interactive "castle" experience at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) annual meeting helped drive 99.8% recall of 5 key messages among participants, and the product saw 33% month-over-month, year-over-year sales growth
  • AI-enabled, human-led. VUE Health uses technology to enhance human expertise rather than replace it, including internal platforms for workflow and resource management, a proprietary capability that assembles custom teams from employees and a network of vetted experts, and AI tools that make scientific dialogue with key opinion leaders faster and more meaningful
  • Focused on what matters most. VUE Health concentrates on emerging biopharma companies in categories where awareness, diagnosis, and clinical education are often the critical barriers. The agency continues to expand its capabilities across media, public relations, technology platforms, and specialized scientific expertise

Kathryn Wilson: Top 10 Inspiring Women Entrepreneurs to Watch in 2026

Wilson founded VUE Health after rising through senior agency roles and finding herself spending less time solving clients' commercialization challenges and more time managing P&Ls and operations. She built VUE Health to return senior talent to the work itself, and that model now defines the agency's identity. MSN's feature highlights her decades of experience translating complex science into clear, meaningful communication for healthcare professionals and patients and a leadership style grounded in integrity, empathy, and meaningful impact. Her path into the industry began with an early pharmaceutical advertising internship that sparked a lasting passion, and today she is committed to supporting communities and developing future women leaders.

"I built the agency because I wanted to get back to the work that brought me into this industry in the first place, helping companies solve difficult challenges and bringing life-changing and lifesaving medicines to market," said Kathryn Wilson, Founder and CEO of VUE Health.

A Recognition Built by the VUE Health Team

"These honors belong to every person at VUE Health," said Wilson. "Agency of the Year recognizes what our team does every day: our medical team, strategists, creatives, media and account leaders, and the vetted experts who partner with us. My own recognition is really a reflection of the people who chose to build something different with me. We are not trying to become the biggest agency. We are focused on becoming the right partner for companies developing therapies where our experience, expertise, and passion can truly make a difference."

Wilson and VUE Health Chief Medical Officer and Partner Vikram Kanda, PhD, a scientist trained in molecular cardiology, work closely with clients as strategic peers, a model especially valuable for emerging biopharma companies whose first commercial hires are often building a launch with limited internal support.

"Pharmaceutical commercialization depends on scientific accuracy, clinical relevance, and a deep understanding of how healthcare decisions are made," said Dr. Kanda. "Our medical team makes sure the science is never separated from the story. That is what this recognition is about: a team that slows down first to understand the science so our clients can move faster later."

VUE Health also thanks:

  • Vikram Kanda, PhD, Partner and Chief Medical Officer and the medical team for best-in-class medical strategy and education
  • Meaghan Taft, SVP Client Service and the strategy and account teams for ensuring commercial excellence
  • Ohad Cohen, Executive Creative Director and the creative team for hard-hitting and targeted creative and pull-through to impact the attention of the HCP
  • Dan Hurley, SVP Innovation and the omnichannel media team for strategic implementation and execution of omnichannel launch excellence and optimization

About VUE Health

VUE Health is an independent healthcare advertising agency that helps emerging biopharma companies bring breakthrough therapies to market. Named Healthcare Advertising Agency of the Year 2026 by Healthcare Business Review, VUE Health pairs dedicated medical directors on every account with senior strategists and creative leaders who stay hands-on from strategy through launch. Its capabilities span medical strategy, brand and creative, omnichannel media, public relations, market access, and proprietary AI-enabled tools, with deep experience in oncology, rare disease, cardiometabolic, hepatology, and CNS. Learn more at vuehealth.com.

Expanded Remit Strengthens Senior Leadership Across Havas Creative & Havas Media in a Priority Growth Market.

NEW YORK, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Havas today announced the promotion of W. Joe DeMiero to CEO, Havas North America, Creative and Media, effective immediately. Reporting jointly to Donna Murphy, Global CEO of Havas Creative Network, and Peter Mears, Global CEO of Havas Media Network, DeMiero will provide senior leadership across both networks in North America, working with leadership to strengthen collaboration and help clients access the breadth of Havas' expertise.

As clients contend with accelerating change driven by AI, data proliferation, evolving consumer expectations, and increasingly interconnected business challenges, leaders are under growing pressure to improve competitiveness and deliver measurable business performance. Building on Havas' established Village approach and its Converged.AI operating model, DeMiero will focus on bringing together the right capabilities across creative, media, production, data and technology, customer experience, social and influencer, and public relations to address those challenges and support client growth.

DeMiero joined Havas Creative Network in May 2026 as Chief Client and Business Officer for North America. Prior to joining Havas, he served as Interim Chief Marketing Officer and subsequently Vice President of Marketing at Sam's Club, where he helped align creative, media, data, and technology investments around enterprise growth priorities. He previously spent more than two decades in senior agency leadership roles, including serving as U.S. CEO of UM and CEO of Publicis Groupe's Hawkeye, with a focus on business transformation, growth acceleration, and strategic client partnerships. 

Yannick Bolloré, Chairman and CEO of Havas, said:

"Clients today are navigating an increasingly complex business environment and are looking for partners who can help them identify growth opportunities, accelerate transformation, and create competitive advantage. Joe's experience on both the client and agency sides of the industry gives him a unique perspective on our clients' needs and how we can best support their ambitions, making him the ideal leader to further strengthen our client-centric approach in North America." 

DeMiero, CEO, Havas North America, Creative & Media, said:

"The strength of Havas has always been our ability to unite great talent around our clients' ambitions. This has led to exceptional growth in North America and strong business performance for Havas globally. Our opportunity now is to make that even easier, helping clients access the full power of the Village to unlock growth, accelerate decision-making, and create measurable business value." 

About Havas

Founded in 1835 in Paris, Havas is one of the world's largest global communications groups, with nearly 23,000 people in over 100 countries. With the ambition to help brands unlock Growth, Powered by Desire, Havas brings together creativity, media, technology and production capabilities to build strong, desirable brands that people genuinely want to engage with. Its integrated model is supported by Converged.AI, the Group's operating system that unifies data, technology and AI to deliver optimized, scalable marketing solutions across the full customer journey. AI-driven, fueled by human ingenuity, and grounded in the belief that desire drives both brand performance and business outcomes, Havas teams collaborate within Havas Villages worldwide to cultivate reputation, relevance and long‑term preference for clients. Havas is equally committed to its people, fostering inclusive, responsible and inspiring workplaces where talent can thrive, because desire also starts from within. Further information is available at www.havas.com.

Veteran media executive joins the business and IT transformation firm as its Media & Entertainment practice scales

NEW YORK, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sol, the leading vendor-neutral firm for AI-enabled business and IT transformation, today announced the appointment of Dan Silberman as Head of Marketing & Communications. Silberman joins the firm after twenty years at A+E Global Media, where he most recently served as Executive Vice President of Communications. He reports to Sol Managing Partner Kaan Aslansan and will be based in New York.

Silberman will own Sol's brand, marketing and communications strategy end to end, covering positioning and narrative, earned media, content and thought leadership, digital presence, internal communications and reputation management, with the work tied to pipeline and growth.  Sol takes enterprise clients from AI strategy to live implementation, including agentic AI systems, workflow modernization and workforce transformation, with a core focus in Media, Entertainment & AdTech, as well as state and local government and education (SLED).

He arrives during the firm's fastest period of expansion. Sol has built out a dedicated AI Acceleration practice under Steve Miller, formerly Chief Digital Officer at Xerox, with former Xerox CEO Steven Bandrowczak as senior advisor, taking clients from diagnosis to live agentic systems. Sol also recently launched its first industry-aligned practice, Media, Entertainment and AdTech, under newly appointed practice lead Ashley J. Swartz.

Silberman joins from A+E Global Media, where he led media relations, corporate and internal communications, crisis management, social strategy and talent relations for The HISTORY Channel, A&E Network, A+E Factual Studios and Oscar-winning feature division A&E IndieFilms, brands reaching more than 400 million households across 200 territories. Earlier, at NBCUniversal, he led press and publicity for Bravo Media, overseeing a full rebrand from its performing-arts roots, launching Queer Eye and Project Runway, and helping transform the network into a pop-culture phenomenon.  He began his career at New York's preeminent public relations firm, Rubenstein Communications, and holds a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy, Politics & Law from Binghamton University. He has been named to The Hollywood Reporter's Next Gen list and Multichannel News' 40 Under 40, received the CableFAX Award for PR Executive of the Year, and serves on the Board of Directors of LMC Media, the largest tri-state area community media center outside of New York City.

"We've built Sol on the strength of our delivery. Now we're investing in making sure the market knows it," said Kaan Aslansan, Managing Partner at Sol. "Dan has built and defended brands under genuine public scrutiny, at a scale most firms never touch. He's exactly what this next phase of growth needs, and he'll make sure the market sees what our clients already do."

"Twenty-five years in television taught me that attention follows the story you tell about your work, not just the work itself," said Silberman. "Sol is competing with firms several times its size and winning, which is the rare case where the story is sitting right there waiting to be told. I'm joining a team of doers that is reshaping how their clients operate, and I'm here to make sure it sounds like it. I've made a career of learning a new business from the best people in it. I want Sol to be the name people already know when we walk in the room."

About Sol

Founded in 2020 and led by Managing Partners Kaan Aslansan, Daniel Gavula, and Carl Graves, Sol is a technology-agnostic business and IT transformation firm that utilizes AI to redesign how companies operate and deliver measurable results, from strategy and operating model design to adoption across the workforce.  Its Sprint 0 discovery process pairs seasoned practitioners with SAGE, Sol's proprietary AI engine, to deliver implementation-ready plans in four to eight weeks rather than the three to six months traditional discovery takes. Sol delivers enterprise AI strategy, agentic AI implementation, workflow modernization, and workforce transformation for clients across industries and public-sector agencies, and measures itself on outcomes rather than recommendations. Learn more at www.wearesol.com.

LOS ANGELES, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- USWC GROUP, INC. U.S. WEED CHANNEL (USWC) today announced the appointment of Larry Namer, co-founder of E! Entertainment Television, as Global Strategy Advisor.

Namer will work with founder Shane Doull to refine the company's global growth strategy, develop its brand-partnership proposition, and position USWC at the intersection of entertainment, cannabis culture, and mainstream consumer marketing.

"Cannabis culture is a starting point for a much broader conversation about entertainment, identity, community, and consumer behavior," said Namer. "The opportunity is not simply to put advertising around cannabis content. It is to build a credible media business that audiences value—and give the right brand partners a meaningful role in that growth."

The appointment comes as USWC advances the Cannabis Center for Advertising Transparency (C-CAT), its public trust initiative giving brands a distinctive role in the platform's development.

A Different Approach to Brand Participation

Rather than treating brands as advertisers buying impressions, USWC developed C-CAT around a more integrated partnership proposition. The initiative connects brand participation with content, audience engagement, and the platform's long-term development.

"Shane's strategic insight is to make category exclusivity part of the business model from the beginning," Namer said. "When the proposition is structured and executed properly, a brand has the opportunity to build a differentiated position—not simply buy another campaign competitors can replicate the following week."

C-CAT's initial outreach drew interest from 390 executives at 209 companies with $10 billion-plus in annual revenue. Its "one partner per category" model means a mega-brand can be 100% locked out by a smaller challenger.

"Size alone does not give a company ownership of an opportunity," Namer added. "A challenger that recognizes the potential and acts decisively may secure a position that a market leader can no longer access on the same terms."

Building for Scale and Credibility

"There's no better mentor I could get. Larry grew E! Entertainment and I get 4 decades of insight." said Doull. "Mega brands call Larry to know 'what's next in entertainment'. He advised Microsoft, brought Hollywood to Russia, and to China. When I shared U.S. WEED CHANNEL he became our Global Strategy Advisor."

"Media history rewards companies that recognize changing audiences before those audiences become an obvious line item in everyone's marketing plan," Namer said. "Our job now is to turn that recognition into a disciplined strategy, a credible audience proposition, and partnerships that make business sense."

To discuss C-CAT participation and category availability, contact Shane Doull at (424) 777-8792, ext. 420, or book an introductory call at https://links.usweedchannel.com/widget/bookings/c-cat-participation.

releases.body:
Employers reach qualified frontline candidates where they already spend their time, and candidates go from a social post to a phone interview in minutes.

NEW YORK, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Classet, the AI phone screener for high-volume hiring, and Reelist, the automated social sourcing platform, today announced a partnership that connects employers with frontline candidates on social media and interviews them within minutes of applying. Together, the two companies give employers a reliable source of qualified, interviewed applicants. Through the integration, customers can source candidates from Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok with one click via Reelist, directly from the Classet platform. Candidates apply in a few taps without ever leaving the app they're scrolling, and Joy, Classet's AI recruiter, calls them within minutes for a structured phone interview.

Candidates go from a social post to an AI phone interview in minutes, with no job board in between.

For employers: Eliminate wasteful job-board spend and hours chasing candidates for interviews.

Teams hiring frontline, skilled trades, and healthcare workers spend most of their recruiting budget on job boards, often with little to show for it. The best workers are usually already employed and not searching job boards, but more than 80% of working adults spend time on social media every day. With Reelist and Classet, employers meet those candidates where they are and have them screened before a recruiter spends a minute on them. Recruiters start the day with candidates who meet their must-have criteria and are ready to schedule.

Reelist customers see up to 3x higher retention and 30% lower cost per hire from social applicants compared with job-board applicants.

And with Classet, employers saw 12% more offers, 18% more starts, and 17% higher retention because Joy surfaces qualified candidates to recruiting teams within minutes.

For candidates: from social post to interview in minutes

Candidates see a job in the feed they already scroll and apply without leaving the app. Instead of waiting days for a callback, they get a phone interview within minutes, day or night, and can ask their own questions about pay, schedule, and the role. They know quickly whether the job is a good fit, and so does the employer. Candidates like it: in Classet's study of 10,167 post-interview ratings, 88% rated their AI phone interview positively.

How it works

  1. Launch from Classet. A recruiter selects the jobs to fill, and with one click, Reelist starts sourcing candidates on social media automatically.
  2. Apply on social media. Candidates see the employer's job in their TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook feed and apply in a few taps.
  3. Interviewed within minutes. Joy calls applicants as soon as they apply, runs the employer's custom phone interview in 25+ languages, answers questions, and flags who meets the must-have criteria. A human makes every hiring decision.
  4. One pipeline. Qualified applicants flow into Classet or into the customer's ATS, with a summary, transcript, and recording for each interview.

From Classet

"Our customers are tired of paying job boards for applicants who never hear back," said Nick Jones, COO and Co-Founder of Classet. "Reelist reaches great candidates where they already are, and Joy interviews them immediately, day or night. Candidates find out fast whether the job is right for them, and recruiters start their morning with people who are qualified and ready to work."

From Reelist

"For years, job boards were the only option for frontline hiring. Not anymore," said Katy Schuck, COO of Reelist. "Employers can recruit qualified workers on social media as easily as posting a job, get every applicant interviewed within minutes, and finally take control of their own hiring."

Availability

The Reelist integration is available now to Classet customers in the platform.

About Reelist

Reelist is the automated social sourcing platform for frontline hiring, from nurses and skilled trades to restaurant general managers. Instead of relying on job board traffic, Reelist puts employers' open roles in front of local candidates on Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok, where they already spend their time. Candidates apply in a few taps, and qualified applicants flow directly into the employer's applicant tracking system, ready for a recruiter to call. Reelist integrates with more than 65 applicant tracking systems and has reached over 10 million job seekers on social media. The company is headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia. Learn more at reelist.com.

About Classet

Classet is the AI recruiting solution for teams hiring hourly, skilled-trades, and frontline workers. Joy, Classet's AI recruiter, calls applicants within moments of applying, day or night, runs a structured phone interview in 25+ languages, and delivers a summary, transcript, and recording for every candidate. Classet Hiring Hub then handles the repetitive work of an ATS, including stage moves, follow-ups, and scheduling, on its own. Joy has interviewed hundreds of thousands of applicants for 500+ hiring teams and connects to 100+ applicant tracking systems. Founded by the team that hired more than one million W2 hourly workers at Bluecrew, Classet is headquartered in Chicago. Learn more at classet.ai.

BEVERLY HILLS, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evolve Media has acquired CafeMom, LittleThings and MamásLatinas, expanding its presence in parenting and lifestyle media.

Evolve Media acquires CafeMom, LittleThings and MamásLatinas, expanding its portfolio of trusted editorial brands.

The brands add trusted editorial destinations and over 40 million combined social media followers. The acquisition creates opportunities to connect with audiences through publications, social media and creator-led content.

"CafeMom, LittleThings and MamásLatinas are iconic digital media properties we've admired for years. Each has built a strong relationship with its audience. Together, they deepen Evolve's connection with moms and families," said Aaron Broder, founder and CEO of Evolve Media. "We're excited to build on that trust with Evolve's broader media capabilities, creating more ways for marketers to connect with these audiences through content and communities they care about."

Each brand brings a distinct voice and audience to Evolve's portfolio:

  • CafeMom provides parents with relatable perspectives, useful information, entertainment and community throughout every stage of motherhood.
  • MamásLatinas delivers culturally relevant parenting, lifestyle and entertainment content for bilingual and bicultural Latina mothers and families.
  • LittleThings shares uplifting lifestyle and human-interest stories designed to inform, inspire and bring people together.

The acquisition advances Evolve's Publisher+ approach, building on established publishing brands and extending their content across social media, video, podcasts and creator partnerships.

CafeMom, LittleThings and MamásLatinas join TotallyKidz and pet brands DogTime and CatTime, helping Evolve connect with families across the moments that shape their lives.

The three brands previously belonged to Wild Sky Media, a digital media company owned by Bright Mountain Technologies. Bright Mountain sold them to Evolve as it shifted its strategic focus to its audience intelligence platform.

"Evolve has been a valued partner to Bright Mountain, collaborating to offer advertising opportunities that reach and engage family audiences. We're glad to see CafeMom, LittleThings and MamásLatinas joining a team we know well," said Matthew Drinkwater, CEO of Bright Mountain.

Evolve plans to build on the strengths of CafeMom, LittleThings and MamásLatinas through added editorial investment while preserving each brand's distinct voice and relationship with its audience.

TORONTO, Oct. 26, 2026 /CNW/ -- Canadian pop culture podcast PopTake, hosted by Hugo Filipe and Mikael Melo, has officially joined Stamina Group's media network through a strategic partnership with View the VIBE. The collaboration brings together two entertainment-focused platforms with a shared passion for culture, community and storytelling, with plans to expand PopTake's reach nationally and explore international distribution opportunities.

Now operating as "PopTake, powered by View the VIBE." Your hot takes on music, pop culture and life. The show will benefit from the publication's established Canadian audience, editorial platform and industry/distribution relationships while maintaining the independent voice and creative chemistry that have become its signature.

The partnership also builds on Stamina Group's experience bringing Canadian-produced content to international audiences. Through its globally distributed video podcast Gents Talk, which has secured placement on airline entertainment systems worldwide and through other transportation syndication partners, Stamina Group has established relationships it hopes to leverage to introduce PopTake to audiences beyond Canada.

"Building Stamina Group has always been about amplifying creative voices and connecting audiences through meaningful content," says Steven Branco, Founder & Chief Creative Officer, Stamina Group Inc. and Editor-in-Chief, View the VIBE. "With PopTake's focus on pop culture and View the VIBE's roots in community, culture and entertainment, the partnership felt like a natural fit. Hugo and Mikael have built something special, and we're excited to help take it further. Building on the international success of Gent's Talk and our global distribution partnerships, we see an opportunity to bring PopTake to audiences across Canada and around the world."

Two best friends, plenty of hot takes

Launched in April 2025, PopTake is a weekly entertainment podcast covering music, film, television, celebrity culture and life. Hosted by longtime friends Hugo Filipe and Mikael Melo, the show combines candid commentary, celebrity interviews and social-first content with the energy of a group chat.

Now in its second season, PopTake has built a growing presence on Canada's entertainment circuit, covering major events including TIFF, the JUNO Awards, the Canadian Screen Awards and Osheaga. Its celebrity interviews have featured the likes of Zara Larsson, Katy Perry, Chloe Bailey, JADE, Perrie Edwards, FLO, Sofi Tukker, Patrick J. Adams, Eric McCormack, Lauren Ash, Simple Plan and Holly Humberstone, and more.

The show also features recognizable segments including Backtrack, where artists identify their songs played backwards; This or That, a rapid-fire celebrity interview format where artists must choose between their own songs; and HotTake or FlopTake, featuring the hosts' weekly pop culture verdicts.

"PopTake started as two best friends who couldn't stop talking about pop culture, so we hit record," says Hugo Filipe, Co-Founder & Co-Host, PopTake. "Partnering with View the VIBE puts our takes in front of an audience that loves this stuff, as much as we do."



"We strike the balance between professional and fanboy," adds Mikael Melo, Co-Founder & Co-Host, PopTake . "Our podcast feels like your two internet besties gushing over your favourite artists, and every now and then, we get to interview them. Asking the questions fans actually want answered."

Beyond the podcast, both hosts bring established entertainment and creative industry experience.

Hugo Filipe is a Toronto-based creative director, photographer and entrepreneur. He leads Mister Mister, a creative studio with clients including H&M, RBC, OVO and Campbell's, and owns Nosso Studio, which operates two creative spaces in Toronto.

Mikael Melo is a Canadian Screen Award-winning producer, reporter and digital creator whose credits include ET Canada, Big Brother Canada and The Social. He has interviewed international stars including Katy Perry, Olivia Rodrigo and Florence Pugh, and collaborated with brands including Paramount+, Samsung, Sony Pictures and Universal Music Canada.

What's next for PopTake?

Through the partnership, PopTake will continue producing its weekly podcast and signature social-first content, while exploring expanded editorial collaborations, new sponsors, celebrity interviews, event coverage, branded entertainment opportunities, in-person events and new distribution channels.

The addition of PopTake further strengthens Stamina Group's growing portfolio of International media properties, which includes View the VIBE, WanderEater, Gent's Post and the internationally distributed and acclaimed video podcast, Gent's Talk.

Every week, the pair deliver fresh perspectives and unfiltered hot takes on the biggest stories in music, film, TV and celebrity culture. Beyond the weekly episode, PopTake has built a reputation for social first interviews and red carpet coverage, from the JUNO Awards and the Canadian Screen Awards to TIFF and Osheaga, with signature segments like Backtrack, This or That and HotTake or FlopTake. BROOKFIELD, Wis., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Best Version Media (BVM), a local media and marketing company serving more than 1,300 communities across the United States and Canada, today announced that Chris Laurence has joined the company as Chief Executive Officer. Kevin O'Brien, who previously served as CEO, will transition to Chief Revenue Officer, focusing on leading BVM's sales field and accelerating revenue growth.

The appointments reflect BVM's investment in leadership to support its next stage of growth. By establishing dedicated executive leadership for the broader organization and the sales field, BVM is strengthening its ability to execute across the business while supporting its independent Publishers and the local businesses they serve.

"Our growth has brought us to a point where leading the overall company and leading our sales field each deserve a dedicated focus," said O'Brien. "This transition allows me to concentrate on working with our sales leaders and Publishers, strengthening the field, and helping more local businesses connect with their communities. I'm excited to partner with Chris as we build on BVM's momentum."

Laurence brings experience as CEO, CFO, and COO of public, private, and private equity-backed companies, where he has led growth, operational improvement, and technology transformation. Before moving into operating roles, he was a general partner at Brentwood Associates, a Los Angeles-based private equity firm.

"BVM has built a powerful combination of community storytelling, local relationships, and marketing solutions for small businesses," said Laurence. "I look forward to working with Kevin and the entire team to build on that foundation, strengthen how we operate, and support the success of our Publishers and clients."

As CEO, Laurence will lead BVM's overall strategy and operations, working with the team to scale operations and support the success of our Publishers and the local businesses they serve. releases.body:
New mural installation by artist A'Darrius Hanible celebrates the country music star as part of the Congress of Country Music's growing public art initiative

PHILADELPHIA, Miss., Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Country music star Lainey Wilson joined GRAMMY Award-winning artist Marty Stuart and community leaders Tuesday for the unveiling of "Wildflowers and Wild Horses," a new mural honoring Wilson in downtown Philadelphia, Mississippi.

"Lainey Wilson is not only a dear friend, but someone who understands the meaning of home," said Marty Stuart. "She knows that no matter how far life takes you or how high your dreams carry you, nothing can replace the people and places that shaped who you are. Lainey came here for this mural unveiling and her fundraiser performances for the Congress of Country Music on nothing more than a hug and a handshake. No contract, no formalities, just friendship, trust and a shared love for where we come from. That tells you everything you need to know about who Lainey Wilson is, and I am so thankful for her support of the Congress of Country Music."

Created by artist A'Darrius Hanible, the mural takes its name and inspiration from Wilson's hit song and celebrates an artist whose distinctive sound, storytelling and authenticity have helped shape a new generation of country music.

The unveiling is part of Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music's ongoing public art initiative, which brings country music's history and cultural influence to life through murals honoring some of the genre's most recognizable artists.

Wilson attended the ceremony and addressed community members and fans gathered to celebrate the new installation.

"This mural is absolutely beautiful, and I'm so grateful the warm welcome I've received here," said Lainey Wilson. "I brought some of my Mississippi friends along for a little picking and grinning, and that's exactly what I want tonight to be about. A chance to step away from the craziness of everyday life, come together and celebrate the heart of country music. At the end of the day, country music is about storytelling, and there's nothing better than sharing those stories with good people."

The mural was made possible through the support of Aalwese Properties, Hill Real Estate, lafedericks.com, Brent and Annette Federick, and the Riviera Motor Hotel, whose contributions reflect the community's continued investment in downtown Philadelphia's growing arts and cultural landscape.

"Wildflowers and Wild Horses" joins a growing collection of murals throughout downtown Philadelphia honoring influential country music artists and songwriters. The initiative builds on the Congress of Country Music's mission to preserve the genre's heritage while creating new opportunities for residents and visitors to experience its enduring influence.

About Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music

Marty Stuart's Congress of Country Music is the spiritual home of country music, committed to touching lives by sharing experiences through exhibits, education and performances that inspire dreams for generations. The Congress aspires to touch lives through a real diversity of offerings in an authentic place unlike any other. Unique live performances, exhibits which honor both legends and newcomers and substantial educational offerings reach audiences across the state and country. Major performing artists are regularly featured alongside a solid season of events, integrated with revolving exhibits in collaboration with the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. Our educational offerings will touch all ages and can be accredited and recognized for their influence.

LIVE TODAY: Tuesday, October 20, 2026 | 12:00 PM ET

WASHINGTON, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CrossCheck Media Inc. today announced that former Major League Baseball pitcher Tanyon Sturtze, who spent 12 seasons in the major leagues, including three with the New York Yankees, will appear live on Franchise Value today at 12:00 PM Eastern Time on Biz Talk Today TV (BTT).

The episode will stream live on the CrossCheck Media YouTube channel and across Biz Talk Today TV's distribution network.

Hosted by Shana Orczyk Sissel, CEO and Founder of Banríon Capital Management and author of Tough Minded, Franchise Value examines the increasingly sophisticated business of professional sports, where franchise valuations, labor negotiations, media rights and financial markets collide.

Today's episode brings an unusually revealing perspective to that conversation.

Sturtze experienced professional baseball from both ends of the financial spectrum. He was an Opening Day starter for the Tampa Bay Devil Rays, one of baseball's lowest-payroll organizations, before joining the New York Yankees and becoming a key member of manager Joe Torre's pitching staff.

His career offers firsthand insight into the financial realities facing professional athletes, from negotiating contracts and competing for roster spots to managing injuries that can abruptly change a player's earning potential.

Now working in the insurance industry, Sturtze brings a second perspective to the business of sports: how athletes, teams and financial institutions evaluate and manage risk.

Baseball's Billion-Dollar Labor Battle

The conversation arrives at a pivotal moment for Major League Baseball.

With the league's collective bargaining agreement scheduled to expire December 1, 2026, owners and players are confronting potentially consequential negotiations over salary caps, minimum payroll requirements, revenue sharing and the possibility of another work stoppage.

At the center of the debate is competitive balance.

The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers are preparing to meet in the World Series despite operating with substantially smaller payrolls than many of baseball's biggest-market franchises.

Their success raises an important question: Does Major League Baseball need a salary cap to create competitive balance, or would a cap primarily give owners greater control over labor costs?

Sissel and Sturtze will explore that question through the experiences of a former player who competed for both a small-market organization and the New York Yankees.

Inside the Yankees Clubhouse

Beyond baseball's labor negotiations, viewers can expect a firsthand look at life inside one of professional sports' most recognizable franchises.

Sturtze will discuss his experiences in the major leagues, the differences between small-market and big-market organizations, and the financial pressures facing players whose careers depend on performance, health and contract negotiations.

The discussion will also examine how injuries can affect an athlete's financial future and why insurance and risk management have become increasingly important components of professional sports.

When Athletes Become Financial Assets

Today's episode will also explore a developing intersection between Wall Street and professional athletics.

From sports-related futures contracts and proposed investment funds to platforms offering investors exposure to athletes' future earnings, financial innovation is creating new ways to participate in the economics of professional sports.

But those developments raise significant questions about regulation, insider information, athlete compensation and financial risk.

Sissel and Sturtze will examine who benefits from these emerging financial products, who bears the risk and whether the athletes themselves are adequately protected.

The conversation will also touch on rising franchise valuations, media-rights economics and the expanding role of institutional capital in professional sports.

releases.title: Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet, and the Stanley Brothers Join Country Music Hall of Fame in Emotional Medallion Ceremony
releases.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tim McGraw, Paul Overstreet and the Stanley Brothers were officially inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame on Sunday, October 18, during the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum's 2026 Medallion Ceremony. But the multiplatinum singer, the ace songwriter, and the bluegrass music pioneers were connected long before they became the 159th, 160th and 161st Hall of Fame members together.

Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum CEO Kyle Young, who led the Medallion Ceremony, recounted in his remarks that McGraw arrived in Nashville at 1 a.m. on May 9, 1989, with a pawn shop guitar and an ambitious dream to make country music. Later that morning, the world learned that the young New Traditionalist singer Keith Whitley had died.

"Now, some people might call that a bad omen," McGraw said during his induction speech. "I've come to believe it was something else. I think Nashville was telling me the truth on my very first day: that this music costs something. The people who make it give everything that they've got. And if you're lucky enough to make it down the road, you owe it to the ones that didn't and the ones who paved it."

Whitley, a 2022 Country Music Hall of Fame inductee, was a student of bluegrass music. Early in his career, he started a band with 2018 inductee Ricky Skaggs that specialized in the repertoire of the Stanley Brothers. Whitley and Skaggs later became members of Ralph Stanley & the Clinch Mountain Boys. Only a few months before he died at age 34, Whitley earned his second #1 single with the song "When You Say Nothing at All," written by Overstreet and 2017 Hall of Fame inductee Don Schlitz.

"I don't believe that's coincidence — I believe that's country music," McGraw said. "It's a chain, and every link holds up the next one."

TIM MCGRAW

With an ear for memorable songs and a musical style that could be both tough and tender, Tim McGraw became one of the most versatile and recognizable country music stars in the 1990s and 2000s. After establishing his music career, he explored acting and landed leading roles in the Hollywood films "The Blind Side," "Country Strong" and "Friday Night Lights," and in the TV series "1883."

"Someday I hope some kid pulls into town with everything they own in a suitcase and a dream too big to fit in it. Maybe they'll hear one of my songs on the radio. And I hope it tells them what I learned from Keith: getting here comes with a cost," a visibly emotional McGraw said as he concluded his speech. "But standing here tonight, in front of all of you, in front of all of my heroes . . . in this moment, tonight, man, it's worth it."

McGraw's list of thank yous began with seven women who helped him reach this career pinnacle: his mother, Betty Ann D'Agostino Trimble; his wife, fellow country singer Faith Hill; his daughters, Audrey, Gracie and Maggie; and his sisters, Sandy and Tracey. Alabama member Randy Owen also focused on McGraw's roots while leading his induction.

"Home has never left his heart. Family has never left his heart. Country music has never left his heart," Owen said. "We're all so lucky that we can call him one of us."

Musical tributes to McGraw included Parker McCollum's heartfelt and faithful version of McGraw's first #1 single, 1994's "Don't Take the Girl"; a sweet rendition of McGraw's 1997 chart-topper, "Just to See You Smile," by Lainey Wilson, who grew up down the road from where McGraw was raised; and Lady A's take on "Live Like You Were Dying," arguably the night's most emotional performance. The trio's Charles Kelley, who was recently diagnosed with a rare blood cancer, sang lead with deep feeling and skill, and bandmates Dave Haywood and Hillary Scott elevated the award-winning crossover hit with their powerful harmony vocals.

"Hearing my songs sung back in your voices is such a strange and beautiful thing," McGraw told them all. "It's like . . . finding a letter you wrote a long time ago and learning it got to where it was going."

PAUL OVERSTREET

A master of catchy melodies and clever, concise wordplay, Paul Overstreet wrote some of the most popular and enduring songs of the 1980s and'90s, including 27 Top Ten country hits between 1981 and 1991 and 13 #1 hits overall. BMI named him Country Songwriter of the Year for an unprecedented five consecutive years (1987 to 1991), and the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame inducted him in 2003.

"Paul took his own ups and downs and turned them into three-minute messages of hope for millions of listeners — title by title, song by song, hit by hit," said Museum CEO Kyle Young. Overstreet's songs brought a modern perspective to time-tested themes: relationships, faith, family, the power of love to unify and heal — and, in the case of a Blake Shelton chart-topper, bad days. Before performing his 2004 single "Some Beach," Shelton told the crowd about how, as a teenager, he idolized Overstreet and, as an aspiring artist, hoped to one day record one of his songs.

"I never dreamed that my Paul Overstreet song would be a song called 'Some Beach,'" he said to laughter, "but damn it, I'm proud of it."

In addition to Shelton's performance, Country Music Hall of Fame member Dean Dillon delivered a song he wrote with Overstreet, "If I Could Bottle This Up," which George Jones recorded in 1988 with Shelby Lynne, while Jamey Johnson's deep and powerful voice proved a perfect match for Randy Travis's 1987 award-winning hit "Forever and Ever, Amen." Overstreet was inducted by Tanya Tucker — whose 1973 concert in Waco, Texas, persuaded Overstreet to move to Nashville to begin his career as a songwriter and singer. Tucker, who recorded Overstreet's composition "I Won't Take Less Than Your Love" with Overstreet and Paul Davis and scored a #1 country hit — praised the songwriter's talent and his heart.

"The brilliant songwriting of Paul Overstreet speaks for itself, but it's Paul Overstreet the friend and the brother that will always be dear to me," she said. In 1988, several months in a rehabilitation program left Tucker uncertain about her life and career, but when she heard "I Won't Take Less Than Your Love" on the radio after leaving the facility, she recalled, "It gave me something to live for and reminded me of the love of a friend that could and would last a lifetime."

THE STANLEY BROTHERS

Before Hall of Fame members Vince Gill and Ricky Skaggs performed the bluegrass standard "Rank Stranger" with guitarist Jeff White, Skaggs said there was nobody happier to see the Stanley Brothers join the Country Music Hall of Fame. Judging by the standing ovations and loud cheers from the crowd throughout the three-hour ceremony, however, that's debatable. Clearly, the induction of brothers Ralph and Carter Stanley, officially performed by Gill, was long awaited by many in attendance.

"This moment has been a lifetime in the making, and it is difficult to put into words what it means to see my father, alongside my Uncle Carter, honored in this way — just the way my daddy wanted it to be — both of them side by side," said Lisa Stanley Marshall, daughter of Ralph Stanley, who represented the Stanley family alongside her brother, Ralph Stanley II, and her cousin, Jeanie Stanley, Carter Stanley's daughter.

"They were the cream of the crop," Jeanie added, "and it has been a long time coming."

Two additional performances in the Stanleys' honor showed just how driving and high-spirited bluegrass can be. Billy Strings and his band earned a standing ovation for their high-octane take on "How Mountain Girls Can Love," full of fast-fingered solos. Similarly, the First Ladies of Bluegrass — Alison Brown, Becky Buller, Sierra Hull, Missy Raines and Molly Tuttle — dazzled with fiery solos on a brisk version of "Bound to Ride." They perform the song with Dolly Parton on a new Stanley Brothers tribute album and added the recordings of Parton's spirited interjections into their live performance.

"Ralph Stanley often rejected the word 'bluegrass' as means of describing the Stanley Brothers' music. It was 'old-time mountain music,' he said, and no one should dare challenge the good doctor on defining his own craft," Museum CEO Kyle Young said. "However, the acoustic instrumentation, the stark lyrics, [and] the blood-resonant harmonies all point to a definitive musical style that is as popular today, eighty years since its commercial inception, [as] ever before."

ABOUT THE MEDALLION CEREMONY

The annual Country Music Hall of Fame Medallion Ceremony is when the year's members-elect officially join their heroes, influences and peers as Hall of Fame members. The celebratory ceremony highlights each new member's talent, achievements and legacy through emotional speeches, surprise musical tributes and video biographies, and a current Hall of Fame member inducts each member-elect.

At the 2026 Medallion Ceremony, the museum's 31st, the Medallion All-Star Band backed many of the night's tribute performances. Led by musical director and acoustic guitarist Biff Watson, the group also included drummer Mark Beckett, keyboard player Jen Gunderman, harmony singer Tania Hancheroff, bassist Alison Prestwood, fiddler and mandolin player Deanie Richardson, pedal steel player Scotty Sanders, acoustic guitarist and harmony singer Jeff White and electric guitarist Charlie Worsham.

At the start of the night, attendees observed a moment of silence in honor of Dolly Parton and Don Schlitz, the two Country Music Hall of Fame members who died within the last year. Patty Loveless, who joined the Hall of Fame in 2023, closed the event with an upbeat performance of "Will the Circle Be Unbroken," altering the lyrics just slightly in tribute to Parton and Schlitz.

The Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum produces the Medallion Ceremony, and the Country Music Association — which elects new Country Music Hall of Fame members —underwrites the event with City National Bank. This is the museum's 31st Medallion Ceremony

About the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum: 

The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum collects, preserves and interprets country music and its history for the education and entertainment of diverse audiences. In exhibitions, publications, digital media and educational programs, the museum explores the cultural importance and enduring beauty of the art form. Among the most-visited history museums in the United States, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum was awarded the country's highest honor in the arts, the National Medal of Arts, in 2024. Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the museum is operated by the Country Music Foundation, a not-for-profit 501(c)(3) educational organization chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964. The Country Music Foundation operates Historic RCA Studio B®, Hatch Show Print® poster shop, Haley Gallery, CMA Theater, CMF Records, the Frist Library and Archive and CMF Press. Museum programs are supported in part by Metro Arts and Tennessee Arts Commission.

More information about the Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum is available at www.countrymusichalloffame.org or by calling (615) 416-2001.

NASHVILLE, Tenn. and COVINGTON, La., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Doussan Music Group (DMG Presents), an independent live entertainment and concert promotion company, is expanding its national presence with the opening of a second office in Nashville, Tennessee, and key leadership appointments.

The new office in Nashville's Wedgewood-Houston neighborhood complements the company's headquarters in Covington, Louisiana, strengthening its connections with artists, agents, venues, and industry partners nationwide.

DMG's expansion follows an extremely successful period of touring and concert promotion. In 2025 and 2026, the company promoted and produced seven college stadium dates featuring The Boys From Oklahoma package, featuring Turnpike Troubadours and Cross Canadian Ragweed, with all shows selling out or nearly selling out. DMG also co promoted Alan Jackson's final touring performance at Nashville's Nissan Stadium, capping Alan's previous two-year, 10-city arena tour. Upcoming engagements include a 16-date fall tour with platinum-selling country artist Jon Pardi and 10 November dates for Aaron Lewis's Acoustic Origins tour. Additional tours planned for 2027 are expected to be announced this fall.

To support its continued growth, DMG has strengthened its leadership team with three personnel updates:

  • Anna Margaret Kilgore joined the company as Talent Buyer in April 2026. With experience in marketing, project management, and touring promotion, she will focus on expanding DMG's event portfolio and building relationships with artists, agencies, and venues.



  • Hale Neitzschman has been named Director of Finance. He will oversee financial operations, event settlements, strategic planning, and financial processes supporting the company's growing touring schedule.



  • Rebecca Saladis has been promoted to Director of Booking, Touring, & Artist Relations. She will lead booking strategy, tour execution, and artist relations.

"Opening our Nashville office, in Wedgewood Houston, the new music hub, is a natural next step in our evolution," said Russell Doussan, President and CEO. He emphasized the company's accomplishments over the past three years and its commitment to working with talented artists to create memorable live music experiences. Founded on artist-first partnerships and exceptional live entertainment, Doussan Music Group continues to expand its concert promotion, tour production, artist relations, and venue partnerships across the country.

releases.body:
The upcoming Toronto conference will bring together clinical research leaders to discuss Canada's competitiveness, innovations in clinical trial design and opportunities to improve patient access to research.

TORONTO, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Xtalks is pleased to announce its role as an official Media Partner for the 2026 CTO Clinical Trials Conference, taking place November 4–5, 2026, at the Hilton Toronto. Hosted by Clinical Trials Ontario (CTO), the two-day event will bring together leaders from the pharmaceutical and medical device industries, healthcare, academia, research institutions and patient organizations to exchange ideas on the future of clinical trials in Canada.

The 2026 conference will explore how Canada can strengthen its position in global clinical research, with discussions on improving trial efficiency, integrating research into patient care and expanding access to clinical trials.

"CTO's Clinical Trials Conference has become one of Canada's most important forums for bringing together diverse voices from across the clinical trials community to share knowledge, challenge thinking and drive innovation," said Susan Marlin, President & CEO, CTO. "We look forward to welcoming delegates and presenters from across Canada and around the world to help shape better, smarter and faster clinical trials that ultimately deliver greater value for patients and participants."

The program will feature keynote presentations from Christine Elliott, former Ontario Minister of Health and Deputy Premier, and Dr. Tor Biering-Sørensen, Professor and Founding Head of the Center for Translational Cardiology and Pragmatic Randomized Trials. Elliott will examine why Canada needs to become more competitive in clinical research and better connect research with patient care, while Dr. Biering-Sørensen will discuss clinical trial innovations from Denmark and the European Union (EU).

Other sessions will address the modernization of clinical trial regulations, the use of AI and health data in research, and efforts to accelerate study start-up. This includes a discussion of early lessons from CTO's QuickSTART initiative, which has demonstrated a 45-day study start-up timeline in its first studies.

Attendees will also gain insights into psilocybin research, including clinical trials underway in Canada and the opportunities and challenges surrounding psychedelic-assisted care.

The agenda will also explore equitable access to clinical trials, Indigenous research sovereignty and approaches to making research more patient-centred. Sessions will examine advance consent in acute stroke trials and how a breast cancer study challenged conventional treatment approaches.

"Having attended last year's CTO Clinical Trials Conference, I was struck by the energy in the room and the thoughtful questions and exchanges among attendees," said Soumya Shashikumar, Senior Life Sciences Journalist at Xtalks. "As a Media Partner, Xtalks looks forward to support this year's discussions on clinical trial innovation, efficiency and patient access."
